ad_as_long_run/lras_sloped.explanation: In the long run output is set by resources and technology, not the price level, so LRAS is vertical at Yf.
ad_as_long_run/lras_sloped.fix: Draw LRAS as a vertical line at Yf.

ad_as_long_run/ad_upward.explanation: Aggregate demand slopes downward: a higher price level lowers real wealth, raises interest rates and makes exports less competitive.

ad_as_long_run/equilibrium_off_lras.explanation: AD and SRAS meet left of LRAS, so output is below Yf: that is a recessionary gap, not long-run equilibrium.
ad_as_long_run/equilibrium_off_lras.fix: Either label it a recessionary gap or draw LRAS through the AD-SRAS intersection.

ad_as_long_run/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'PL' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Real GDP' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

ad_as_long_run/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

ad_as_long_run/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

ad_as_long_run/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'LRAS' and 'AD' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as lras is labeled 'AD', and the curve drawn as aggregate demand is labeled 'LRAS'.
ad_as_long_run/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'LRAS' goes on the lras curve and 'AD' on the aggregate demand curve.

ad_as_output_gap/gap_mislabeled.explanation: Output Y₂ is above full employment, which is a inflationary gap.

ad_as_output_gap/ad_shift_wrong_directio.explanation: 'An export boom' increases aggregate demand, so AD should shift right.
ad_as_output_gap/ad_shift_wrong_directio.fix: Draw AD₂ to the right of AD₁.

ad_as_output_gap/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price level (PL)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Real GDP (Y)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

ad_as_output_gap/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

ad_as_output_gap/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

ad_as_output_gap/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'LRAS' and 'SRAS' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as lras is labeled 'SRAS', and the curve drawn as sras is labeled 'LRAS'.
ad_as_output_gap/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'LRAS' goes on the lras curve and 'SRAS' on the sras curve.

budget_line_shift/income_drawn_as_pivot.explanation: A pure income increase with unchanged prices keeps the slope (−Px/Py), so the line shifts out in parallel; both intercepts move.

budget_line_shift/price_drawn_as_paralle.explanation: Only the price of pizza changed, so the soda intercept (income/Py) stays fixed; the line pivots out along the pizza axis.
budget_line_shift/price_drawn_as_paralle.fix: Keep the soda intercept and move only the pizza intercept.

budget_line_shift/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

budget_line_shift/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

business_cycle/peak_trough_swapped.explanation: The high point of the cycle is the peak and the low point is the trough; they are labeled backwards.

business_cycle/phase_labels_swapped.explanation: Between these turning points real GDP is falling, so this phase is a contraction.

business_cycle/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Real GDP' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Time' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

business_cycle/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

comparative_advantage/comparative_advant.explanation: Comparative advantage goes to the lower opportunity cost. Country B gives up less clothing per unit of food (flatter PPF).
comparative_advantage/comparative_advant.fix: Country B has the comparative advantage in food.

comparative_advantage/missing_axis_label.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

comparative_advantage/missing_curve_labe.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

consumer_optimum/optimum_not_tangent.explanation: At E the indifference curve crosses the budget line, so MRS ≠ Px/Py. The consumer can reach a higher indifference curve by reallocating spending.
consumer_optimum/optimum_not_tangent.fix: Move the optimum to where the highest reachable curve is tangent to the line.

consumer_optimum/curves_crossing.explanation: Indifference curves cannot cross: the crossing point would give two different utility levels, violating transitivity.
consumer_optimum/curves_crossing.fix: Draw the curves so that none of them intersect.

consumer_optimum/curves_concave.explanation: Indifference curves are drawn concave to the origin. Diminishing MRS makes them convex (bowed toward the origin); with concave curves, the tangency point is a utility minimum.
consumer_optimum/curves_concave.fix: Redraw the curves bowed toward the origin.

consumer_optimum/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

consumer_optimum/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

consumer_optimum/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'Budget line' and 'IC₁' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as budget is labeled 'IC₁', and the curve drawn as indifference curve is labeled 'Budget line'.
consumer_optimum/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'Budget line' goes on the budget curve and 'IC₁' on the indifference curve curve.

consumer_producer_surplus/cs_ps_swapped.explanation: The labels are reversed. Consumer surplus is the triangle under demand and above price; producer surplus is above supply and below price.
consumer_producer_surplus/cs_ps_swapped.fix: Label the upper triangle CS and the lower triangle PS.

consumer_producer_surplus/cs_shaded_as_r.explanation: The shaded rectangle P*×Q* is total consumer spending, not consumer surplus.
consumer_producer_surplus/cs_shaded_as_r.fix: Shade the triangle between the demand curve and the price line P*, from 0 to Q*.

consumer_producer_surplus/axis_labels_sw.explanation: 'Price (P)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity (Q)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

consumer_producer_surplus/missing_axis_l.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

consumer_producer_surplus/missing_curve_.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

consumer_producer_surplus/curve_labels_s.explanation: The labels 'D' and 'S' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'S', and the curve drawn as supply is labeled 'D'.
consumer_producer_surplus/curve_labels_s.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D' goes on the demand curve and 'S' on the supply curve.

cost_curves/mc_misses_atc_min.explanation: MC must cross ATC and AVC at their minimum points: when marginal cost is below average, the average falls; when above, it rises.
cost_curves/mc_misses_atc_min.fix: Redraw MC so it passes through the lowest points of AVC and ATC.

cost_curves/atc_avc_labels_swapped.explanation: ATC = AVC + AFC, so ATC must lie above AVC. The labels are reversed.
cost_curves/atc_avc_labels_swapped.fix: Label the higher U-shaped curve ATC and the lower one AVC.

cost_curves/afc_rising.explanation: Average fixed cost = FC/Q always falls as output rises, since a fixed amount is spread over more units.
cost_curves/afc_rising.fix: Draw AFC as a downward-sloping curve that approaches the axis.

cost_curves/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Costs' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity (Q)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

cost_curves/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

cost_curves/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

demand_shift/shift_wrong_direction.explanation: 'Price of a substitute for wheat rises' should shift demand to the right, but the new curve is drawn to the left.
demand_shift/shift_wrong_direction.fix: Redraw D₂ to the right of D₁; equilibrium price rises and quantity rises.

demand_shift/wrong_curve_shifted.explanation: 'Price of a substitute for wheat rises' is a demand-side change, but the graph shifts the supply curve instead.
demand_shift/wrong_curve_shifted.fix: Keep supply fixed and shift the demand curve right.

demand_shift/new_equilibrium_misplaced.explanation: E₂ is drawn at the old price on the new curve, not where the new curve meets the unchanged curve. The market would not clear there.
demand_shift/new_equilibrium_misplaced.fix: Place E₂ at the intersection of the shifted curve and the curve that did not move.

demand_shift/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price ($)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

demand_shift/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

demand_shift/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

demand_shift/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D₁' and 'S' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'S', and the curve drawn as supply is labeled 'D₁'.
demand_shift/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D₁' goes on the demand curve and 'S' on the supply curve.

elasticity_comparison/elasticity_labels_.explanation: The labels are reversed. Through the same point, the steeper demand curve is relatively inelastic and the flatter one relatively elastic.
elasticity_comparison/elasticity_labels_.fix: Label the steep curve inelastic and the flat curve elastic.

elasticity_comparison/axis_labels_swappe.explanation: 'Price (P)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity (Q)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

elasticity_comparison/missing_axis_label.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

elasticity_comparison/missing_curve_labe.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

fx_market/fx_wrong_direction.explanation: 'Demand for ¥-area exports rises' increases demand for ¥, so the demand curve should shift right.

fx_market/fx_label_wrong.explanation: The price of ¥ in $ rose, so the ¥ appreciated.

fx_market/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: '$ per ¥' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity of ¥' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

fx_market/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

fx_market/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

fx_market/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D¥₁' and 'S¥' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as currency demand is labeled 'S¥', and the curve drawn as currency supply is labeled 'D¥₁'.
fx_market/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D¥₁' goes on the currency demand curve and 'S¥' on the currency supply curve.

is_lm/is_lm_labels_swapped.explanation: IS (goods market equilibrium) slopes downward and LM (money market equilibrium) slopes upward; the labels are reversed.

is_lm/policy_wrong_curve.explanation: Government spending is a goods-market change: it shifts IS, not LM.

is_lm/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'i' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Real GDP (Y)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

is_lm/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

is_lm/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

isoquant_isocost/optimum_not_tangent.explanation: At E the isoquant crosses the isocost, so MRTS ≠ w/r. The same cost could produce more output.
isoquant_isocost/optimum_not_tangent.fix: Move the optimum to where the highest reachable curve is tangent to the line.

isoquant_isocost/curves_crossing.explanation: Isoquants cannot cross: one input bundle cannot produce two different output levels.
isoquant_isocost/curves_crossing.fix: Draw the curves so that none of them intersect.

isoquant_isocost/curves_concave.explanation: Isoquants should be convex to the origin (diminishing MRTS).
isoquant_isocost/curves_concave.fix: Redraw the curves bowed toward the origin.

isoquant_isocost/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

isoquant_isocost/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

isoquant_isocost/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'Isocost' and 'Q₁' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as isocost is labeled 'Q₁', and the curve drawn as isoquant is labeled 'Isocost'.
isoquant_isocost/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'Isocost' goes on the isocost curve and 'Q₁' on the isoquant curve.

keynesian_cross/ae_slope_above_one.explanation: AE has slope equal to the MPC, which is between 0 and 1, so AE must be flatter than the 45° line and cross it from above.
keynesian_cross/ae_slope_above_one.fix: Draw AE with a positive intercept and slope < 1.

keynesian_cross/equilibrium_off_45.explanation: E is on the AE line but not on the 45° line, so planned spending exceeds output there and inventories fall; output will rise.
keynesian_cross/equilibrium_off_45.fix: Move E to where AE crosses the 45° line.

keynesian_cross/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Aggregate expenditure (AE)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Income, output (Y)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

keynesian_cross/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

keynesian_cross/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

keynesian_cross/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels '45° line (AE = Y)' and 'AE = C + I + G + NX' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as 45 degree is labeled 'AE = C + I + G + NX', and the curve drawn as aggregate expenditure is labeled '45° line (AE = Y)'.
keynesian_cross/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: '45° line (AE = Y)' goes on the 45 degree curve and 'AE = C + I + G + NX' on the aggregate expenditure curve.

laffer_curve/revenue_positive_at_100.explanation: At a 100% tax rate there is no incentive to earn taxable income, so revenue falls to zero.
laffer_curve/revenue_positive_at_100.fix: Bring the curve back down to zero at 100%.

laffer_curve/revenue_monotonic.explanation: This curve keeps rising. The Laffer curve rises, peaks at some rate t*, then falls to zero at 100%.
laffer_curve/revenue_monotonic.fix: Draw an inverted U from 0% to 100%.

laffer_curve/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Tax revenue' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Tax rate (%)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

laffer_curve/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

loanable_funds/lf_wrong_direction.explanation: More government borrowing increases demand for loanable funds, shifting D right.
loanable_funds/lf_wrong_direction.fix: Shift the curve to the right.

loanable_funds/lf_wrong_curve.explanation: A deficit means more government borrowing: the demand curve shifts, not supply.

loanable_funds/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Real interest rate (r)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity of loanable funds' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

loanable_funds/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

loanable_funds/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

loanable_funds/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'S_LF' and 'D_LF₁' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as supply lf is labeled 'D_LF₁', and the curve drawn as demand lf is labeled 'S_LF'.
loanable_funds/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'S_LF' goes on the supply lf curve and 'D_LF₁' on the demand lf curve.

lorenz_curve/lorenz_above_equality.explanation: A Lorenz curve can never lie above the line of equality: the poorest x% cannot earn more than x% of income.
lorenz_curve/lorenz_above_equality.fix: Draw the Lorenz curve bowed below the 45° line.

lorenz_curve/gini_area_mislabeled.explanation: The area under the Lorenz curve is B. The inequality area A is between the line of equality and the Lorenz curve.
lorenz_curve/gini_area_mislabeled.fix: Shade the gap between the two curves as A.

lorenz_curve/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Cumulative % of income' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Cumulative % of population' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

lorenz_curve/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

lorenz_curve/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

lorenz_curve/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'Line of equality' and 'Lorenz curve' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as line of equality is labeled 'Lorenz curve', and the curve drawn as lorenz curve is labeled 'Line of equality'.
lorenz_curve/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'Line of equality' goes on the line of equality curve and 'Lorenz curve' on the lorenz curve curve.

minimum_wage/min_wage_below_equilibrium.explanation: A minimum wage below the equilibrium wage is non-binding; the market wage stays at W* and there is no unemployment from it.
minimum_wage/min_wage_below_equilibrium.fix: Draw a binding minimum wage above W*.

minimum_wage/unemployment_measured_wrong.explanation: Unemployment is the gap between labor supplied and labor demanded at the minimum wage (Ls − Ld), not Ls − L*.
minimum_wage/unemployment_measured_wrong.fix: Measure the gap from Ld to Ls.

minimum_wage/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Wage (W)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Labor (L)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

minimum_wage/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

minimum_wage/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

minimum_wage/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D_L = MRP' and 'S_L' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as labor demand is labeled 'S_L', and the curve drawn as labor supply is labeled 'D_L = MRP'.
minimum_wage/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D_L = MRP' goes on the labor demand curve and 'S_L' on the labor supply curve.

money_market/ms_upward.explanation: The money supply is set by the central bank and does not respond to the interest rate, so MS is vertical.

money_market/ms_shift_wrong_direction.explanation: 'The central bank lowers the reserve requirement' increases the money supply, so MS shifts right and i falls.

money_market/axis_real_rate.explanation: The money market graph uses the nominal interest rate (the opportunity cost of holding money); the real rate belongs on the loanable funds graph.
money_market/axis_real_rate.fix: Label the vertical axis 'Nominal interest rate (i)'.

money_market/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Nominal interest rate (i)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity of money (M)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

money_market/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

money_market/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

money_market/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'MD' and 'MS₁' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as money demand is labeled 'MS₁', and the curve drawn as money supply is labeled 'MD'.
money_market/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'MD' goes on the money demand curve and 'MS₁' on the money supply curve.

monopolistic_competition_lr/tangent_at_m.explanation: A monopolistically competitive firm faces downward-sloping demand, so the tangency must be on the downward-sloping part of ATC, left of the minimum (excess capacity).
monopolistic_competition_lr/tangent_at_m.fix: Draw D tangent to ATC to the left of min ATC.

monopolistic_competition_lr/lr_profit_sh.explanation: Demand lies above ATC, so firms earn economic profit. With free entry, that cannot persist in the long run.
monopolistic_competition_lr/lr_profit_sh.fix: Shift D (and MR) left until D is just tangent to ATC.

monopolistic_competition_lr/axis_labels_.explanation: 'Price, cost' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Q' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

monopolistic_competition_lr/missing_axis.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

monopolistic_competition_lr/missing_curv.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

monopolistic_competition_lr/curve_labels.explanation: The labels 'ATC' and 'MC' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as average total cost is labeled 'MC', and the curve drawn as marginal cost is labeled 'ATC'.
monopolistic_competition_lr/curve_labels.fix: Swap the labels back: 'ATC' goes on the average total cost curve and 'MC' on the marginal cost curve.

monopoly/price_read_from_mr.explanation: The monopolist charges the highest price consumers will pay for Qm, which is on the demand curve, not at the MR = MC point.
monopoly/price_read_from_mr.fix: Go up from Qm to D and read Pm there.

monopoly/mr_parallel_to_demand.explanation: With linear demand P = a − bQ, MR = a − 2bQ: same intercept, twice as steep. MR cannot be parallel to demand.
monopoly/mr_parallel_to_demand.fix: Draw MR starting at the demand intercept and hitting the quantity axis halfway to demand's intercept.

monopoly/quantity_where_d_meets_mc.explanation: Q where D = MC is the competitive outcome. A monopolist restricts output to where MR = MC.
monopoly/quantity_where_d_meets_mc.fix: Find Qm at MR = MC, then read Pm from demand; shade the DWL.

monopoly/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

monopoly/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

monopoly/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

monopoly/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D = AR' and 'MR' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'MR', and the curve drawn as marginal revenue is labeled 'D = AR'.
monopoly/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D = AR' goes on the demand curve and 'MR' on the marginal revenue curve.

monopsony/wage_read_from_mfc.explanation: The monopsonist pays the lowest wage workers will accept for Lm, which is on the supply curve, not the MFC = MRP point.
monopsony/wage_read_from_mfc.fix: Drop from the MRP = MFC point down to S and read Wm there.

monopsony/mfc_below_supply.explanation: Marginal factor cost exceeds the wage for a monopsonist (raising the wage applies to all workers), so MFC lies above S and is steeper.
monopsony/mfc_below_supply.fix: Draw MFC above S with the same intercept and twice the slope.

monopsony/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Wage (W)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Labor (L)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

monopsony/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

monopsony/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

monopsony/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'S = AFC' and 'MFC' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as labor supply is labeled 'MFC', and the curve drawn as marginal factor cost is labeled 'S = AFC'.
monopsony/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'S = AFC' goes on the labor supply curve and 'MFC' on the marginal factor cost curve.

negative_externality/social_curve_wrong_.explanation: With a negative externality, social cost exceeds private cost, so MSC must lie above MPC, not below.
negative_externality/social_curve_wrong_.fix: Draw MSC above S = MPC by the external cost per unit.

negative_externality/q_labels_swapped.explanation: The market quantity is where D meets MPC and the social optimum is where D meets MSC; with a negative externality the market overproduces, so Qm > Qs.
negative_externality/q_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the Qm and Qs labels.

negative_externality/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price (P)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity (Q)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

negative_externality/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

negative_externality/missing_curve_label.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

negative_externality/curve_labels_swappe.explanation: The labels 'D = MPB = MSB' and 'S = MPC' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'S = MPC', and the curve drawn as private cost is labeled 'D = MPB = MSB'.
negative_externality/curve_labels_swappe.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D = MPB = MSB' goes on the demand curve and 'S = MPC' on the private cost curve.

pc_firm_loss/loss_labeled_profit.explanation: ATC at q* is above the price, so the firm earns an economic loss, not a profit.

pc_firm_loss/shutdown_claim_wrong.explanation: The shutdown rule compares P with AVC, not ATC. Since P > min AVC, producing loses less than shutting down (which loses all fixed costs).
pc_firm_loss/shutdown_claim_wrong.fix: The firm should keep operating in the short run; shut down only if P < min AVC.

pc_firm_loss/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price, cost ($)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Output (q)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

pc_firm_loss/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

pc_firm_loss/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

pc_firm_loss/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'MC' and 'ATC' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as marginal cost is labeled 'ATC', and the curve drawn as average total cost is labeled 'MC'.
pc_firm_loss/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'MC' goes on the marginal cost curve and 'ATC' on the average total cost curve.

pc_firm_profit/output_at_min_atc.explanation: Output is set at the minimum of ATC. A profit-maximizing firm produces where MR = MC, which is to the right of min ATC when P is above it.
pc_firm_profit/output_at_min_atc.fix: Move q* to where P = MC on the rising MC curve.

pc_firm_profit/profit_height_uses_avc.explanation: The profit rectangle is measured down to AVC (which ignores fixed costs). Economic profit is (P − ATC) × q.
pc_firm_profit/profit_height_uses_avc.fix: Draw the bottom of the profit rectangle at ATC(q*).

pc_firm_profit/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: '$' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Output (q)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

pc_firm_profit/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

pc_firm_profit/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

pc_firm_profit/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'MC' and 'ATC' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as marginal cost is labeled 'ATC', and the curve drawn as average total cost is labeled 'MC'.
pc_firm_profit/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'MC' goes on the marginal cost curve and 'ATC' on the average total cost curve.

pc_firm_profit/output_where_mc_falling.explanation: q* is at the crossing on the falling part of MC; there, producing more adds profit. The profit maximum is where MC crosses MR from below.
pc_firm_profit/output_where_mc_falling.fix: Use the MC = MR crossing on the upward-sloping part of MC.

pc_long_run/lr_price_above_atc_min.explanation: Price is above min ATC, so firms earn positive economic profit. That attracts entry, so it cannot be a long-run equilibrium.
pc_long_run/lr_price_above_atc_min.fix: In long-run equilibrium P = MR = MC = min ATC.

pc_long_run/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'P, C' belongs on the vertical axis and 'q' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

pc_long_run/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

pc_long_run/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

pc_long_run/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'MC' and 'ATC' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as marginal cost is labeled 'ATC', and the curve drawn as average total cost is labeled 'MC'.
pc_long_run/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'MC' goes on the marginal cost curve and 'ATC' on the average total cost curve.

per_unit_subsidy/subsidy_shifts_supply_u.explanation: A subsidy lowers producers' effective cost, shifting supply down (right). Shifting it up shows a tax.
per_unit_subsidy/subsidy_shifts_supply_u.fix: Draw S − subsidy below S; price to buyers falls and quantity rises.

per_unit_subsidy/dwl_wrong_side.explanation: With a subsidy, output rises past Q*. The deadweight loss comes from overproduction between Q* and Qs, to the right of E.
per_unit_subsidy/dwl_wrong_side.fix: Shade the triangle between E, (Qs,Pp) and (Qs,Pc).

per_unit_subsidy/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

per_unit_subsidy/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

per_unit_subsidy/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

per_unit_subsidy/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D' and 'S' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'S', and the curve drawn as supply is labeled 'D'.
per_unit_subsidy/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D' goes on the demand curve and 'S' on the supply curve.

per_unit_tax/tax_shifts_supply_down.explanation: A tax on sellers raises their cost per unit, shifting supply up (left) by the tax. Shifting it down shows a subsidy.
per_unit_tax/tax_shifts_supply_down.fix: Draw S + tax above S by the amount of the tax; Pc rises, Qt falls.

per_unit_tax/dwl_wrong_side.explanation: The deadweight loss is drawn beyond Q*. A tax reduces trade, so the lost surplus is between Qt and Q*, to the left of the original equilibrium.
per_unit_tax/dwl_wrong_side.fix: Shade the triangle with vertices (Qt,Pc), (Qt,Pp) and E.

per_unit_tax/revenue_uses_original_quant.explanation: Tax revenue is tax × quantity actually sold after the tax (Qt), not the pre-tax Q*.
per_unit_tax/revenue_uses_original_quant.fix: Make the revenue rectangle width Qt.

per_unit_tax/producer_price_at_old_equil.explanation: Pp is drawn at the old equilibrium price. Sellers receive Pc minus the tax, which is the height of the original supply curve at Qt.
per_unit_tax/producer_price_at_old_equil.fix: Read Pp off the original S at Qt.

per_unit_tax/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price ($)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

per_unit_tax/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

per_unit_tax/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

per_unit_tax/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D' and 'S' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'S', and the curve drawn as supply is labeled 'D'.
per_unit_tax/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D' goes on the demand curve and 'S' on the supply curve.

perfect_elasticity/perfect_labels_swappe.explanation: A horizontal demand curve is perfectly elastic and a vertical one is perfectly inelastic; the labels are reversed.

perfect_elasticity/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price ($)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

perfect_elasticity/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

perfect_elasticity/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

phillips_curve/srpc_upward.explanation: The short-run Phillips curve slopes downward: lower unemployment comes with higher inflation in the short run.

phillips_curve/lrpc_not_at_natural_rate.explanation: The LRPC must be vertical at the natural rate uₙ; here it sits at a different unemployment rate, so the long-run point A is off the LRPC.

phillips_curve/axes_swapped_phillips.explanation: The Phillips curve puts the inflation rate on the vertical axis and the unemployment rate on the horizontal axis.

phillips_curve/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

phillips_curve/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

phillips_curve/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'SRPC' and 'LRPC' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as srpc is labeled 'LRPC', and the curve drawn as lrpc is labeled 'SRPC'.
phillips_curve/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'SRPC' goes on the srpc curve and 'LRPC' on the lrpc curve.

positive_externality/social_curve_wrong_.explanation: With a positive externality, social benefit exceeds private benefit, so MSB must lie above MPB.

positive_externality/q_labels_swapped.explanation: With a positive externality the market underproduces: Qm (D meets S) is less than Qs (MSB meets S). The labels are reversed.
positive_externality/q_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the Qm and Qs labels.

positive_externality/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'P' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Q' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

positive_externality/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

positive_externality/missing_curve_label.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

positive_externality/curve_labels_swappe.explanation: The labels 'D = MPB' and 'MSB' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as private benefit is labeled 'MSB', and the curve drawn as social benefit is labeled 'D = MPB'.
positive_externality/curve_labels_swappe.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D = MPB' goes on the private benefit curve and 'MSB' on the social benefit curve.

ppf/ppf_bowed_in.explanation: The PPF is bowed in (convex). Increasing opportunity cost requires a bowed-out (concave) frontier: each extra unit of X costs more Y.
ppf/ppf_bowed_in.fix: Redraw the PPF bowed outward from the origin.

ppf/point_labels_wrong.explanation: Points on the frontier are efficient and points inside are inefficient; A and B are labeled the wrong way around.
ppf/point_labels_wrong.fix: Label A efficient and B inefficient.

ppf/outside_point_attainable.explanation: C lies outside the PPF, so it cannot be produced with current resources and technology.

ppf/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

ppf_shift/shift_inward.explanation: 'Investment adds to the capital stock' expands production possibilities, so the PPF must shift outward, not inward.

ppf_shift/pivot_vs_parallel.explanation: The technology only affects pizza, so the maximum amount of robots does not change. The PPF should pivot out along the pizza axis.
ppf_shift/pivot_vs_parallel.fix: Keep the robots intercept fixed and move only the pizza intercept out.

ppf_shift/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

ppf_shift/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

price_ceiling/ceiling_above_equilibrium.explanation: The ceiling is above the equilibrium price, so it is non-binding: the market still clears at P*, with no shortage.
price_ceiling/ceiling_above_equilibrium.fix: A binding ceiling must be drawn below P*; otherwise remove the gap label.

price_ceiling/labeled_surplus.explanation: At a binding price ceiling quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, so the gap is a shortage, not a surplus.
price_ceiling/labeled_surplus.fix: Relabel the gap as a shortage.

price_ceiling/qs_qd_swapped.explanation: Qs and Qd are swapped: quantity supplied is read off the supply curve and quantity demanded off the demand curve.
price_ceiling/qs_qd_swapped.fix: Label the quantity where the control line meets S as Qs and where it meets D as Qd.

price_ceiling/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'P' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Q' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

price_ceiling/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

price_ceiling/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

price_ceiling/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D' and 'S' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'S', and the curve drawn as supply is labeled 'D'.
price_ceiling/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D' goes on the demand curve and 'S' on the supply curve.

price_floor/floor_below_equilibrium.explanation: The floor is below the equilibrium price, so it is non-binding: the market still clears at P*, with no surplus.
price_floor/floor_below_equilibrium.fix: A binding floor must be drawn above P*; otherwise remove the gap label.

price_floor/labeled_shortage.explanation: At a binding price floor quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, so the gap is a surplus, not a shortage.
price_floor/labeled_shortage.fix: Relabel the gap as a surplus.

price_floor/qs_qd_swapped.explanation: Qs and Qd are swapped: quantity supplied is read off the supply curve and quantity demanded off the demand curve.
price_floor/qs_qd_swapped.fix: Label the quantity where the control line meets S as Qs and where it meets D as Qd.

price_floor/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price ($)' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

price_floor/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

price_floor/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

price_floor/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D' and 'S' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'S', and the curve drawn as supply is labeled 'D'.
price_floor/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D' goes on the demand curve and 'S' on the supply curve.

short_run_production/mp_misses_ap_max.explanation: When MP > AP, AP rises; when MP < AP, AP falls. So MP must cross AP exactly at AP's peak.
short_run_production/mp_misses_ap_max.fix: Redraw MP through the top of AP.

short_run_production/mp_ap_labels_swappe.explanation: The curve that peaks earlier and falls faster (eventually below zero) is MP; the flatter one it crosses at the peak is AP. Labels are reversed.
short_run_production/mp_ap_labels_swappe.fix: Swap the MP and AP labels.

short_run_production/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'MP, AP' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Labor (L)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

short_run_production/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

short_run_production/missing_curve_label.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

solow_growth/steady_state_off_intersecti.explanation: At the marked k, investment exceeds break-even investment, so capital per worker is still growing. Steady state is where sf(k) crosses (n + δ)k.

solow_growth/output_investment_swapped.explanation: Investment per worker sf(k) is a fraction (s < 1) of output, so it must lie below f(k); the labels are swapped.
solow_growth/output_investment_swapped.fix: Label the higher curve f(k) and the lower one sf(k).

solow_growth/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Output, investment per worker' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Capital per worker (k)' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

solow_growth/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

solow_growth/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

supply_demand_equilibrium/demand_slopes_.explanation: The demand curve slopes upward. By the law of demand, quantity demanded falls as price rises, so demand must slope downward.
supply_demand_equilibrium/demand_slopes_.fix: Redraw D from the upper left to the lower right through E.

supply_demand_equilibrium/equilibrium_of.explanation: E is placed on the demand curve but not where demand and supply cross. At that price quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, so it is not an equilibrium.
supply_demand_equilibrium/equilibrium_of.fix: Move E to the intersection of D and S and re-read P* and Q*.

supply_demand_equilibrium/curve_labels_s.explanation: The downward-sloping curve is labeled S and the upward-sloping curve D. Demand slopes down and supply slopes up.
supply_demand_equilibrium/curve_labels_s.fix: Swap the labels: the downward-sloping curve is D, the upward-sloping curve is S.

supply_demand_equilibrium/axis_labels_sw.explanation: 'P' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Q' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

supply_demand_equilibrium/missing_axis_l.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

supply_demand_equilibrium/missing_curve_.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

supply_shift/shift_wrong_direction.explanation: 'New technology lowers the cost of producing smartphones' should shift supply to the right, but the new curve is drawn to the left.
supply_shift/shift_wrong_direction.fix: Redraw S₂ to the right of S₁; equilibrium price falls and quantity rises.

supply_shift/wrong_curve_shifted.explanation: 'New technology lowers the cost of producing smartphones' is a supply-side change, but the graph shifts the demand curve instead.
supply_shift/wrong_curve_shifted.fix: Keep demand fixed and shift the supply curve right.

supply_shift/new_equilibrium_misplaced.explanation: E₂ is drawn at the old price on the new curve, not where the new curve meets the unchanged curve. The market would not clear there.
supply_shift/new_equilibrium_misplaced.fix: Place E₂ at the intersection of the shifted curve and the curve that did not move.

supply_shift/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'Price' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Quantity' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

supply_shift/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

supply_shift/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

supply_shift/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D' and 'S₁' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'S₁', and the curve drawn as supply is labeled 'D'.
supply_shift/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D' goes on the demand curve and 'S₁' on the supply curve.

supply_shock/sras_shift_wrong_direction.explanation: 'Oil prices spike' raises costs of production, so SRAS should shift left.

supply_shock/called_demand_pull.explanation: Inflation caused by a leftward SRAS shift is cost-push inflation (with lower output: stagflation). Demand-pull inflation comes from AD shifting right.

supply_shock/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'PL' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Real GDP' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

supply_shock/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

supply_shock/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

supply_shock/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'AD' and 'SRAS₁' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as aggregate demand is labeled 'SRAS₁', and the curve drawn as sras is labeled 'AD'.
supply_shock/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'AD' goes on the aggregate demand curve and 'SRAS₁' on the sras curve.

tariff/tariff_lowers_price.explanation: A tariff is a tax on imports; it raises the domestic price above the world price, not below it.
tariff/tariff_lowers_price.fix: Draw Pw + tariff above Pw. Domestic quantity supplied rises and imports shrink.

tariff/revenue_rectangle_wrong.explanation: Tariff revenue is collected only on imports after the tariff (Qs₂ to Qd₂), not on free-trade imports.
tariff/revenue_rectangle_wrong.fix: Shrink the revenue rectangle to span Qs₂–Qd₂ between Pw and Pw + tariff.

tariff/imports_from_origin.explanation: Imports are the gap between domestic quantity demanded and domestic quantity supplied, not total quantity demanded.
tariff/imports_from_origin.fix: Measure imports from Qs₂ to Qd₂.

tariff/axis_labels_swapped.explanation: 'P' belongs on the vertical axis and 'Q' on the horizontal axis; the axis labels are swapped, which reverses the meaning of every slope.

tariff/missing_axis_labels.explanation: Neither axis is labeled, so the curves cannot be interpreted.

tariff/missing_curve_labels.explanation: None of the curves are labeled, so it is ambiguous which is which.

tariff/curve_labels_swapped.explanation: The labels 'D' and 'S (domestic)' are on the wrong curves: the curve drawn as demand is labeled 'S (domestic)', and the curve drawn as supply is labeled 'D'.
tariff/curve_labels_swapped.fix: Swap the labels back: 'D' goes on the demand curve and 'S (domestic)' on the supply curve.
